fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar eased to 0.7276 against the U.S. dollar, down 0.6% on the week and up 1.6% year-over-year, with USD/CAD at 1.3743 — driven by the wide Bank of Canada–Federal Reserve policy gap, which held the loonie soft even as WTI crude traded near US$100/bbl19. The Bank of Canada's 2.25% policy rate sits roughly 138 basis points below the Federal Reserve's 3.50%-3.75% target midpoint after both central banks held in late April, a differential that continued to favour U.S.-dollar carry over crude-linked Canadian-dollar support123. EUR/USD slipped 0.8% on the week to 1.1640, though it remained 3.6% above its year-ago level, as Bloomberg-surveyed economists positioned for two ECB quarter-point hikes in 2026 against the energy-driven inflation backdrop28. USD/JPY rose 1.1% to 158.49 and stands 9.3% above a year ago, while USD/CNY was little changed at 6.81. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the softer loonie to the 83 manufacturing projects valued at $129.0B exposed to cross-border trade. If the loonie holds near its current soft level against the greenback through the CUSMA review window, those 83 trade-exposed manufacturing projects would face the input-cost and tariff conditions documented in the March merchandise trade data. CAD/USD at 0.7276 frames that exposure13.

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada curve held a normal, upward slope, with the 2Y at 2.96% and the 10Y at 3.56% for a 2s10s spread of about 60 basis points — steeper than the roughly 49 basis points recorded a year ago, reflecting global term-premium repricing as the synchronized G7 central-bank hold met an energy-driven inflation regime29. Prior-week tenor levels were unavailable, so moves are measured against year-ago levels. Against a year ago, the 2Y is up about 39 basis points from 2.57% and the 10Y up about 50 basis points from 3.06%, with the Long bond up roughly 61 basis points to 3.91% — the steepest year-over-year back-up on the curve. The Bank of Canada's fourth consecutive hold at 2.25% on April 29 anchored the front end while ECB tightening expectations and the BoE's second consecutive hold pushed the global long end higher127. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the rate path to 1,663 infrastructure projects ($210.3B) and 211 residential projects ($32.2B) carrying rate-sensitive financing exposure. If the yields tracked here hold near current levels rather than retreating, those rate-sensitive infrastructure and residential projects, totalling roughly two hundred forty billion dollars with commercial-adjacent exposure, would carry financing costs consistent with the held policy rate rather than the lower term yields seen a year earlier3.
